en: A public sale in which things are sold to the person who offers the most money; or to sell this way.
ex: The painting was sold at auction for a million dollars.
這幅畫以一百萬元的價格拍賣售出。

en: Strong disagreement with a plan or idea; or the political party that is not in power.
ex: There was strong opposition to the new tax.
人們強烈反對這項新稅。

en: Not interested in or not caring about something.
ex: He seemed indifferent to the results of the election.
他似乎對選舉結果漠不關心。

en: Based on ideas and principles rather than practical experience.
ex: The plan is theoretical and has not been tested.
這個計畫只是理論上的，還沒有經過測試。

en: Able to be reached, entered or used; or easy to understand.
ex: The museum is accessible to people in wheelchairs.
博物館對輪椅使用者無障礙通行。

en: A person who fights in the sport of boxing; or a medium-sized dog breed.
ex: The boxer won the match in the third round.
那位拳擊手在第三回合贏得比賽。

en: A set of moral principles; or the study of right and wrong.
ex: Doctors must follow a strict code of ethics.
醫生必須遵守嚴格的倫理守則。

en: To surprise someone very much.
ex: Her sudden resignation astonished everyone in the office.
她突然辭職讓辦公室裡所有人都很驚訝。

en: A young person who is developing from a child into an adult.
ex: Adolescents often struggle to find their identity.
青少年常常難以找到自己的身分認同。

en: According to what people believe, often without proof.
ex: The restaurant is supposedly the best in town.
據說這家餐廳是鎮上最好的。

en: The number of deaths in a particular group or time; or the fact that all humans must die.
ex: Infant mortality has fallen sharply in recent decades.
近幾十年來嬰兒死亡率大幅下降。

en: To make a copy of something in order to deceive; or to form something by heating and shaping metal.
ex: He was arrested for forging his boss's signature.
他因偽造老闆的簽名而被捕。

en: To agree to do a task or responsibility; or to begin to do something.
ex: The firm will undertake the repair work next month.
公司將在下個月承接維修工程。

en: To officially declare that someone is guilty of a crime; or a person in prison.
ex: The jury convicted him of fraud.
陪審團判他詐欺罪名成立。

en: To officially give something, such as money or time, to a particular person or purpose.
ex: The city allocated money for a new library.
市政府撥款興建一座新圖書館。

en: The rate at which goods are produced or work is done, compared with the effort used.
ex: New machines have greatly improved the factory's productivity.
新機器大大提高了工廠的生產力。

en: A person who takes part in an activity or event.
ex: All participants will receive a certificate.
所有參加者都會收到一張證書。

en: To organize different people or things so they work well together; or one of the numbers that give a position on a map.
ex: She coordinates the volunteers at the event.
她負責協調活動中的志工。

en: A set of rooms in a hotel; or a set of related things such as furniture or software.
ex: We booked a suite with a view of the ocean.
我們訂了一間可以看海景的套房。

en: A large pink fish that swims up rivers to lay eggs; or the meat of this fish.
ex: Salmon swim upstream to lay their eggs.
鮭魚逆流而上去產卵。

en: To take something quickly and roughly; or a short part of something.
ex: A thief snatched her handbag and ran away.
一名小偷搶了她的手提包後逃走。

en: A particular way of thinking about a subject.
ex: Try to see the problem from the customer's viewpoint.
試著從顧客的角度看這個問題。

en: A statement in which someone admits they have done something wrong or a crime.
ex: The suspect made a full confession to the police.
嫌犯向警方全盤招供。

en: A piece of soft cloth or paper worn by a baby to take in waste.
ex: She changed the baby's diaper before bed.
她睡前幫寶寶換了尿布。

en: One of the curved bones around the chest; or to tease someone in a friendly way.
ex: He fell off the bike and broke two ribs.
他從腳踏車上摔下來，斷了兩根肋骨。

en: The outer edge of something circular, such as a cup, glass or wheel.
ex: The glass was filled right up to the rim.
玻璃杯被倒滿到杯緣。

en: To show or prove that a decision or action is reasonable or necessary.
ex: Nothing can justify such violence.
任何事都不能為這種暴力辯解。

en: The work of keeping and checking the financial records of a business.
ex: He studied accounting at university.
他在大學主修會計。

en: A set of actions done in a fixed order, especially as part of a religious or social ceremony.
ex: Drinking tea every afternoon is a family ritual.
每天下午喝茶是一種家庭儀式。

en: A feeling of respect mixed with fear or wonder.
ex: The children gazed in awe at the giant waterfall.
孩子們敬畏地凝視著那座巨大的瀑布。

en: A small group of people who work or train together, such as in the police or army.
ex: The bomb squad arrived within minutes.
拆彈小組幾分鐘內就趕到了。

en: To make someone familiar with something; or to make yourself know something well.
ex: You should acquaint yourself with the safety rules.
你應該熟悉安全規定。

en: To state exactly what is needed or must be done.
ex: Please specify your size when you place the order.
下訂單時請註明你的尺寸。

en: A student in the second year of high school or college, in the US.
ex: She is a sophomore majoring in biology.
她是主修生物的大二學生。

en: To deliberately not include something or someone; or to keep someone out of a place or group.
ex: The price excludes tax and delivery costs.
價格不含稅和運費。

en: A covered area at the entrance of a house, often with a roof.
ex: We sat on the porch and watched the rain.
我們坐在門廊上看雨。

en: A fixed number or amount of something that is officially allowed.
ex: The factory must meet its monthly quota.
工廠必須達成每月配額。

en: To cut away small parts of something to make it neat; or neat and tidy.
ex: He trimmed his beard before the interview.
他在面試前修剪了鬍子。

en: To shine brightly with small points of light; or a quality of liveliness and brightness.
ex: The lake sparkled in the morning sun.
湖水在晨光中閃閃發光。

en: Having the right to do or receive something because you meet the conditions.
ex: Only citizens over eighteen are eligible to vote.
只有年滿十八歲的公民才有資格投票。
